Chapter 1: Arrays — Section 1
An array stores elements in contiguous memory. Indexed access is normally O(1). Searching an unsorted array is O(n).
Insertion or deletion in the middle may require shifting elements and is generally O(n).
In this section, students study arrays through definitions, operations, implementation choices, applications, and complexity.
The important rule is to connect each operation to its cost as input size grows. This section is intentionally repeated with
different review wording so a retrieval system must search across a large document.
